subject: general
question: A and B can do a piece of work in 13 days and 52 days, respectively. Both work for 2 days and then A goes away. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(13, 52) = 52 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 4 units/day, Efficiency of **B** = 1 unit/day.

Work done in 2 days = (4 + 1) × 2 = 10 units.

Remaining work = 52 − 10 = 42 units.

Time taken by **B** for remaining work = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 13 days, Time taken by **B** = 52 days.

⇒ Total efficiency of (**A** + **B**) = 4 + 1 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Work completed in 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 52 − 10 = 42 units.

⇒ Time taken by **B** to complete remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of **B**

⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is similar to time and work where filling a tank is positive work and emptying it (leakage) is negative work.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual or their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p
